question: True or false: a radon atom that has already lasted a month is more likely to decay this week than a newly formed one?
answer: False. A nucleus does not wear out: a radon-222 atom a month old has the same 50% chance of decaying in the next 3.8 days as one just formed. A sample shrinks because atoms leave it, not because survivors age. Uranium atoms older than the Earth decay at the rate they did when forged.
move: Ask whether a thing can wear out before calling it overdue.
trap: Treating an old atom like an old machine, near the end.
source: Institute of Physics, IOPSpark, decay constant
